claim: In Ogataea polymorpha, the position of pre-anaphase nucleus is not strongly biased toward bud neck, unlike in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
source: Here we show that unlike the best-studied yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae, position of pre-anaphase nucleus is not strongly biased toward bud neck in Ogataea polymorpha and the regulation of spindle positioning becomes active only shortly before anaphase.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and related figures.

claim: The regulation of spindle positioning in O. polymorpha becomes active only shortly before anaphase.
source: Here we show that unlike the best-studied yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae, position of pre-anaphase nucleus is not strongly biased toward bud neck in Ogataea polymorpha and the regulation of spindle positioning becomes active only shortly before anaphase.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by time-lapse microscopy data in Figure 1E and related figures.

claim: The unstable property of cMTs in O. polymorpha compared to S. cerevisiae is likely responsible for the lack of nuclear positioning bias.
source: This is likely due to the unstable property of cMTs compared to those in S. cerevisiae.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 2 showing cMT instability.

claim: cMT nucleation/anchoring in O. polymorpha is restricted at the level of recruitment of Spc72 to the spindle pole body.
source: Furthermore, we show that cMT nucleation/anchoring is restricted at the level of recruitment of the γ-tubulin complex receptor, Spc72, to spindle pole body (SPB), which is regulated by the polo-like kinase Cdc5.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 4 and 5 showing cell cycle-dependent Spc72 localization.

claim: Spc72 recruitment to SPB in O. polymorpha is regulated by the polo-like kinase Cdc5.
source: Furthermore, we show that cMT nucleation/anchoring is restricted at the level of recruitment of the γ-tubulin complex receptor, Spc72, to spindle pole body (SPB), which is regulated by the polo-like kinase Cdc5.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 6, 7, and 8 showing Cdc5-dependent Spc72 recruitment.

claim: The cytoplasmic side of SPB in O. polymorpha is structurally different between G1 and anaphase.
source: Additionally, electron microscopy revealed that the cytoplasmic side of SPB is structurally different between G1 and anaphase.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by electron microscopy images in Figure 3.

claim: Polo-like kinase dependent recruitment of γ-tubulin receptor to SPBs determines the timing of spindle orientation in O. polymorpha.
source: Thus, polo-like kinase dependent recruitment of γ-tubulin receptor to SPBs determines the timing of spindle orientation in O. polymorpha.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, synthesizing the findings from multiple experiments.

claim: The nucleus is positioned close to the bud neck in large budded pre-anaphase cells of S. cerevisiae.
source: The nucleus is positioned close to the bud neck in large budded pre-anaphase cells of S. cerevisiae (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Similar nuclear organization to S. cerevisiae was observed in Candida glabrata, Kluyveromyces lactis, Pichia pastoris, and Yarrowia lipolytica.
source: Similar organization was observed in other budding yeast species including Candida glabrata, Kluyveromyces lactis, Pichia pastoris, and Yarrowia lipolytica (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: In O. polymorpha, nuclear position was not biased to the bud neck in pre-anaphase cells.
source: Notably in O. polymorpha, however, nuclear position was not biased to the bud neck, although it remained in the mother cell body (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The nucleus was located in the cell centre in 76.7% of G2/M cells in O. polymorpha.
source: Close examination of O. polymorpha revealed that the nucleus was located in the cell centre in 76.7% of G2/M cells whereas in the remainder of the cells it was off-centred with no bias towards the bud neck (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The nuclear position is not determined before anaphase onset in O. polymorpha.
source: These results suggest that the nuclear position is not determined before anaphase onset in O. polymorpha.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in Figure 1A and related figures.

claim: The early stages of anaphase occurred in the mother cell body in O. polymorpha.
source: As a consequence, the early stages of anaphase occurred in the mother cell body (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: 97.4% of early anaphase spindles in O. polymorpha were located entirely in the mother cell body.
source: Majority of the early anaphase spindles as judged according to their length (<5 µm) as well as a stretched DNA mass were located entirely in the mother cell body (97.4%, Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claim: 94.7% of early anaphase spindles in O. polymorpha were aligned along the bud-mother axis.
source: However, 94.7% of the early anaphase spindles were aligned along the bud-mother axis and almost all of the late anaphase spindles with two segregated DNAs were inserted into the bud (Figure 1—figure supplement 3), suggesting immediate and efficient orientation of the spindle during anaphase.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Almost all late anaphase spindles with two segregated DNAs in O. polymorpha were inserted into the bud.
source: However, 94.7% of the early anaphase spindles were aligned along the bud-mother axis and almost all of the late anaphase spindles with two segregated DNAs were inserted into the bud (Figure 1—figure supplement 3), suggesting immediate and efficient orientation of the spindle during anaphase.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: SPBs in O. polymorpha were duplicated at the timing of bud emergence or later.
source: Two SPB signals appeared in some of small/medium budded cells (Figure 1D, panel c, lower cell), suggesting that SPBs were duplicated at the timing of bud emergence or later, which is similar to that in S. cerevisiae although the precise cell cycle stage should be carefully determined.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Intensity of Mps3-GFP in medium/large-budded cells with a single SPB was much higher than that in unbudded G1 cells or cells with separated SPBs.
source: Consistent with this, intensity of Mps3-GFP in medium/large-budded cells with a single SPB was much higher than that in unbudded G1 cells or cells with separated SPBs (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: SPB in G1 cells and small budded cells of O. polymorpha was not in a defined position within the mother cell body.
source: Moreover, SPB in G1 cells as well as small budded cells was not in the defined position within the mother cell body (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: After spindle assembly in O. polymorpha, ~1 µm long spindles remained at their central positions and loosely oriented toward the bud neck until shortly before anaphase onset.
source: Subsequent time lapse analysis revealed that after spindle assembly, ~1 µm long spindles remained at their central positions and loosely oriented toward the bud neck until shortly before anaphase onset (defined by the rapidly increase of pole-to-pole distance) (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: Anaphase in O. polymorpha initiated in the mother cell body.
source: Anaphase initiated in the mother cell body (Figure 1E, 11 min, Figure 1—figure supplement 6, 3–4 min).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 6.

claim: Spindle alignment in O. polymorpha was corrected around the time of (or shortly after) spindle elongation.
source: Spindle alignment was corrected around the time of (or shortly after) spindle elongation, followed by SPB insertion into the bud.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by time-lapse data in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 6.

claim: After spindle breakdown in O. polymorpha, the SPB moved vigorously with no relationship to the polarity axis.
source: After spindle breakdown, the SPB moved vigorously with no relationship to the polarity axis (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 6.

claim: cMTs were observed in all anaphase cells of O. polymorpha.
source: cMTs were observed in all anaphase cells, whereas less than 50% of G1 and pre-anaphase cells carried cMTs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Less than 50% of G1 and pre-anaphase cells in O. polymorpha carried cMTs.
source: cMTs were observed in all anaphase cells, whereas less than 50% of G1 and pre-anaphase cells carried cMTs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: cMTs that apparently did not associate with the SPB were observed in 13.8% of O. polymorpha cells prior to anaphase.
source: Furthermore, cMTs that apparently did not associate with the SPB were observed in 13.8% of cells prior to anaphase (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Detached cMTs in O. polymorpha remained in the cytoplasm for only a short period of time before depolymerizing.
source: Time lapse analysis revealed that detached cMTs remained in the cytoplasm for only a short period of time before depolymerized (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: In S. cerevisiae, almost all cells exhibit cMTs that are stably associated with the SPB during the cell cycle.
source: This situation is in stark contrast to that in S. cerevisiae where almost all cells exhibit cMTs that are stably associated with the SPB during the cell cycle (Shaw et al., 1997; Kosco et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: cMTs in O. polymorpha were observed during 20.6% of the recorded time points in time lapse experiments.
source: To test these possibilities, we performed time lapse experiments with cells expressing GFP-TUB1, in which cMTs were observed during 20.6% of the recorded time points although the majority (>80%) did not persist longer than 30 s (Figure 2D, cMT persistence, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The majority (>80%) of cMTs in O. polymorpha did not persist longer than 30 s.
source: To test these possibilities, we performed time lapse experiments with cells expressing GFP-TUB1, in which cMTs were observed during 20.6% of the recorded time points although the majority (>80%) did not persist longer than 30 s (Figure 2D, cMT persistence, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: cMTs in O. polymorpha are short-lived during early stages of the cell cycle.
source: These results suggest that cMTs are short-lived during early stages of the cell cycle.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in Figure 2D.

claim: Once cMTs were lost in O. polymorpha, a relatively long time was required until new MTs appeared at the SPB (median value 90.0 s, average 173.8 ± 192.4 s).
source: Once cMTs were lost, a relatively long time was required until new MTs appeared at the SPB (Figure 2D, cMT re-establishment; median value 90.0 s, average 173.8 ± 192.4 s).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: cMTs in O. polymorpha are less frequently nucleated and unstable at early stages of the cell cycle.
source: Thus, cMTs are less frequently nucleated and unstable at early stages of the cell cycle.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in Figure 2D.

claim: Acquired cMTs efficiently corrected the spindle orientation in pre-anaphase cells of O. polymorpha.
source: Acquired cMTs efficiently corrected the spindle orientation in pre-anaphase cells, suggesting that the spindle orientation is regulated largely at the level of cMT acquisition (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Spindle orientation in O. polymorpha is regulated largely at the level of cMT acquisition.
source: Acquired cMTs efficiently corrected the spindle orientation in pre-anaphase cells, suggesting that the spindle orientation is regulated largely at the level of cMT acquisition (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Anaphase SPBs in O. polymorpha had an additional thin layer in the cytoplasm that resembled the outer plaque of S. cerevisiae SPB.
source: Anaphase SPBs had an additional thin layer in the cytoplasm that resembled the outer plaque of S. cerevisiae SPB (Figure 3A and B) (Byers and Goetsch, 1974; Byers and Goetsch, 1975).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: There was no detectable outer plaque in G1 SPBs of O. polymorpha.
source: In contrast, there was no detectable outer plaque in G1 SPBs (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: O. polymorpha SPBs undergo structural cycling in every cell cycle.
source: These results suggested that O. polymorpha SPBs undergo structural cycling in every cell cycle.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the electron microscopy data presented in Figure 3.

claim: All six side-by-side SPBs in O. polymorpha had outer plaques.
source: All six side-by-side SPBs had outer plaques which were similar to that in nocodazole arrested cells, albeit some of those were somewhat fuzzy.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The SPB structure on cytoplasmic side in O. polymorpha is reconstructed before spindle formation.
source: The result suggested that the SPB structure on cytoplasmic side is reconstructed before spindle formation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the electron microscopy data of side-by-side SPBs in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: An additional electron dense cloud was observed on the cytoplasmic side of nuclear envelope between two SPB bodies in O. polymorpha, which resembled the half-bridge/bridge structure of S. cerevisiae SPB.
source: An additional electron dense cloud was observed on the cytoplasmic side of nuclear envelope between two SPB bodies, which resembled the half-bridge/bridge structure of S. cerevisiae SPB (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B and E; orange arrowheads).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Putative orthologues of genes for Mps3, Sfi1, Spc72, Spc110, and Nud1 as well as γ-TuSC components, Tub4, Spc97, and Spc98 were identified in the O. polymorpha genome.
source: BLAST and HMMER searches have identified putative orthologues of genes for Mps3, Sfi1, Spc72, Spc110, and Nud1 as well as γ-TuSC components, Tub4, Spc97, and Spc98 in the O. polymorpha genome (Altschul et al., 1990; Sobel and Snyder, 1995; Geissler et al., 1996; Knop and Schiebel, 1997; Eddy, 1998; Maekawa and Kaneko, 2014; Riley et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations to bioinformatics tools and databases.

claim: GFP or mRFP dot-like signals of Tub4, Spc98, Mps3, Sfi1, and Nud1 were observed in most O. polymorpha cells, suggesting they represent constitutive components of the SPB throughout the cell cycle.
source: GFP or mRFP dot-like signals of Tub4, Spc98, Mps3, Sfi1, and Nud1 were observed in most of the cells, suggesting that they represent constitutive components of the SPB throughout the cell cycle (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Spc72 signal in O. polymorpha was either weak or absent in cells at early cell cycle stages, whereas all anaphase cells carried two strong SPB signals.
source: In contrast, the Spc72 signal was either weak or absent in cells at early cell cycle stages, whereas all anaphase cells carried two strong SPB signals (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: SPC72 is essential for growth in O. polymorpha.
source: These results suggested that SPC72 is essential for growth in O. polymorpha.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by tetrad dissection analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The GFP signal of Spc72 in O. polymorpha was 2.5 times weaker in cells with a short spindle than in anaphase cells (p<0.001).
source: The GFP signal was 2.5 times weaker in cells with a short spindle than in anaphase cells (p<0.001).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Nud1 in O. polymorpha did not show cell cycle-dependent changes in SPB localization intensity.
source: In contrast, Nud1, which comprises the putative binding site of Spc72 on the outer plaque as suggested by the direct interaction between orthologues of these proteins in S. cerevisiae, did not show this trend, nor did Sfi1, a half-bridge component (Figure 4B) (Gruneberg et al., 2000; Kilmartin, 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Sfi1, a half-bridge component in O. polymorpha, did not show cell cycle-dependent changes in SPB localization intensity similar to Nud1.
source: In contrast, Nud1, which comprises the putative binding site of Spc72 on the outer plaque as suggested by the direct interaction between orthologues of these proteins in S. cerevisiae, did not show this trend, nor did Sfi1, a half-bridge component (Figure 4B) (Gruneberg et al., 2000; Kilmartin, 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Spc72 is cell cycle regulated and the incorporation of Spc72 into SPBs may be the key step to stabilize cMTs in O. polymorpha.
source: These results suggest that Spc72 is cell cycle regulated and the incorporation of Spc72 into SPBs may be the key step to stabilize cMTs.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in Figure 4B.

claim: In all O. polymorpha cells that progressed into anaphase, an Spc72-GFP signal became detectable <4 min prior to the initiation of anaphase (average 3.68 ± 1.74 min, n = 14).
source: In all cells that progressed into anaphase, an Spc72-GFP signal became detectable <4 min prior to the initiation of anaphase (average 3.68 ± 1.74 min, n = 14) (Figure 4C, orange arrowheads).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Within 5 min after appearance of the Spc72-GFP signal in O. polymorpha, spindle orientation was corrected when it had not done already (average 3.50 ± 1.61 min, n = 12).
source: Within 5 min after appearance of the Spc72-GFP signal, spindle orientation was corrected when it had not done already (Figure 4—figure supplement 3, average 3.50 ± 1.61 min, n = 12); therefore, one half part of an anaphase nucleus was successfully inserted into the bud.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Spc72 accumulates at SPB in early mitosis, most likely in metaphase, and remains high during anaphase in O. polymorpha.
source: Thus, Spc72 accumulates at SPB in early mitosis, most likely in metaphase, and remains high during anaphase.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the time-lapse data presented in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: As O. polymorpha cells exit from mitosis and enter the next cell cycle, Spc72-GFP signal was gradually decreased at SPBs with the timing that varied from cell to cell.
source: As cells exit from mitosis and entre the next cell cycle, Spc72-GFP signal was gradually decreased at SPBs with the timing that varied from cell to cell.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by time-lapse data in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: In all cases, Spc72-GFP levels in O. polymorpha reached a minimum well before short spindle was formed.
source: However, in all cases, Spc72-GFP levels reached a minimum well before short spindle was formed (Figure 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: Overexpressed Spc72-GFP was efficiently targeted to SPB in O. polymorpha because a strong Spc72-GFP signal was observed in cells carrying the PTEF1-SPC72-GFP gene but not in wild-type cells during G1 and G2/M phases.
source: Overexpressed Spc72-GFP was efficiently targeted to SPB because a strong Spc72-GFP signal was observed in cells carrying the PTEF1-SPC72-GFP gene but not in wild-type cells during G1 and G2/M phases (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: In O. polymorpha cells overexpressing SPC72-GFP, SPB was positioned close to the bud neck.
source: In cells overexpressing SPC72-GFP, SPB was positioned close to the bud neck, which is reminiscent of the SPB position in S. cerevisiae (Figures 1A and 5B), and cMTs were more often observed (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figures 1A, 5B, 5C, and 5D.

claim: cMTs were more often observed in O. polymorpha cells overexpressing SPC72-GFP.
source: In cells overexpressing SPC72-GFP, SPB was positioned close to the bud neck, which is reminiscent of the SPB position in S. cerevisiae (Figures 1A and 5B), and cMTs were more often observed (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: cMT organization in O. polymorpha is regulated at the level of repeated Spc72 recruitment to the SPB in every cell cycle.
source: Together, these results strongly supported our hypothesis that cMT organization is regulated at the level of repeated Spc72 recruitment to the SPB in every cell cycle.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the overexpression experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: While Spc72 was accumulated at SPBs in nutrient starved O. polymorpha cells, cMTs were not observed.
source: Interestingly, while Spc72 was accumulated at SPBs, cMTs were not observed (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Specific mechanism may regulate Spc72 and cMT organization under nutrient starvation conditions in O. polymorpha.
source: Thus, specific mechanism may regulate Spc72 and cMT organization under such conditions.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Spc72 protein abundance in O. polymorpha did not fluctuate as cells entered into anaphase and proceeded into the following cell cycle.
source: Spc72 protein abundance did not fluctuate as cells entered into anaphase and proceeded into the following cell cycle (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The Spc72 band in O. polymorpha migrated slower in nocodazole-arrested cells than that in asynchronous cells.
source: Furthermore, the Spc72 band migrated slower in nocodazole-arrested cells than that in asynchronous cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Either post-translational modification of Spc72 or regulation of Spc72 binding proteins might be utilized to achieve cell cycle dependency of SPB localisation in O. polymorpha.
source: These results suggested that either post-translational modification of Spc72 or regulation of Spc72 binding proteins might be utilized to achieve cell cycle dependency of SPB localisation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The GFP intensity of Spc72-GFP at the SPB in O. polymorpha was significantly lower in cells arrested by Cdc5-depletion than that in cells after re-accumulation of Cdc5 in both metaphase (SPB distance <2 µm, p<0.0001) and anaphase (SPB distance >4 µm, p<0.0001).
source: Furthermore, we noticed that the GFP intensity of Spc72-GFP at the SPB was significantly lower in cells arrested by Cdc5-depletion than that in cells after re-accumulation of Cdc5 in both metaphase (SPB distance <2 µm, p<0.0001) and anaphase (SPB distance >4 µm, p<0.0001) (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: Strong dependency of SPB binding of Spc72 on Cdc5 was confirmed in metaphase-arrested O. polymorpha cells by nocodazole.
source: Strong dependency of SPB binding of Spc72 on Cdc5 was further confirmed in metaphase-arrested cells by nocodazole (Figure 6D, Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The stable association of Spc72 in O. polymorpha requires Cdc5 kinase, the activity of which is likely cell cycle-regulated.
source: These results suggested that the stable association of Spc72 requires Cdc5 kinase, the activity of which is likely cell cycle-regulated.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in Figure 6B, C, and D.

claim: Spc72 is phosphorylated by Cdc5 kinase in S. cerevisiae.
source: Spc72 is phosphorylated by Cdc5 kinase in S. cerevisiae (Maekawa et al., 2007; Snead et al., 2007), which prompted us to investigate whether Spc72 is subjected to a Cdc5-dependent phosphorylation in O. polymorpha.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Spc72 of O. polymorpha is subjected to post-translational modifications in a Cdc5-dependent manner.
source: Our gel electrophoresis analyses of nocodazole-arrested cells suggested that Spc72 of O. polymorpha is subjected to post-translational modifications in a Cdc5-dependent manner because the Spc72 band was more smeared and migrated slightly slower in wild type and CDC5-overexpressing cells as compared to that in Cdc5-depleted cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3A.

claim: λ-phosphatase treatment revealed in vivo phosphorylation of Spc72 in O. polymorpha that was independent of Cdc5.
source: Although this difference was largely lost during preparation of cell extract, the λ-phosphatase treatment revealed in vivo phosphorylation of Spc72 that was independent of Cdc5 (Figure 6—figure supplement 3B), suggesting that Cdc5 contributes to a subset of phosphorylations of Spc72.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Cdc5 contributes to a subset of phosphorylations of Spc72 in O. polymorpha.
source: Although this difference was largely lost during preparation of cell extract, the λ-phosphatase treatment revealed in vivo phosphorylation of Spc72 that was independent of Cdc5 (Figure 6—figure supplement 3B), suggesting that Cdc5 contributes to a subset of phosphorylations of Spc72.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in Figure 6—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Spc72 in O. polymorpha is phosphorylated at multiple sites, only some of which depend on Cdc5.
source: Thus, Spc72 is phosphorylated at multiple sites, only some of which depend on Cdc5.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: Distinctive localization of Cdc5-GFP in O. polymorpha became apparent after S phase and was lost prior to or during the following G1 phase.
source: Distinctive localization of Cdc5-GFP became apparent after S phase and was lost prior to or during the following G1 phase (Figure 7A and B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7A, B, and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Nuclear and NE localisation of Cdc5 in O. polymorpha appeared at early stages of the cell cycle and persisted until the end of mitosis.
source: Nuclear and NE localisation appeared at early stages of the cell cycle and persisted until the end of mitosis.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: A fraction of the Cdc5-GFP signals in O. polymorpha appeared to overlap with those of SPBs during mitosis.
source: In addition, a fraction of the GFP signals appeared to overlap with those of SPBs during mitosis.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: Neither NE nor SPB-associated Cdc5-GFP signals were detected in unbudded or small budded O. polymorpha cells.
source: Neither NE nor SPB-associated GFP signals were detected in unbudded or small budded cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: Spc72-GFP and Spc110-tdTomato signals in O. polymorpha were clearly distinguished in 58% of the cells by structured illumination microscopy.
source: Spc72-GFP and Spc110-tdTomato signals were clearly distinguished in 58% of the cells, which verified that our method could discriminate signals in the cytoplasmic and the nuclear side of SPB in >50% of cells (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Cdc5-GFP overlapped with Spc110-tdTomato in 53% of O. polymorpha cells.
source: Cdc5-GFP overlapped with Spc110-tdTomato in 53% of cells, which is similar to the degree of co-localisation observed between Spc72 and Spc110.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The Cdc5-GFP signal overlapped with Spc72-tdTomato in 87% of O. polymorpha cells.
source: In contrast, the Cdc5-GFP signal overlapped with Spc72-tdTomato in 87% of cells (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Cdc5-GFP in O. polymorpha locates at the position on SPBs closer to Spc72 than to Spc110, indicating that Cdc5-GFP signal arises from the cytoplasmic side of SPB.
source: These results suggest that Cdc5-GFP locates at the position on SPBs closer to Spc72 than to Spc110, indicating that Cdc5-GFP signal arises from the cytoplasmic side of SPB.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structured illumination microscopy data presented in Figure 7D.

claim: Cdc5 in O. polymorpha likely becomes first localised to the nucleus and the NE in G2, and then in mitosis to the cytoplasmic side of SPBs.
source: Thus, Cdc5 likely becomes first localised to the nucleus and the NE in G2, and then in mitosis to the cytoplasmic side of SPBs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the localization data presented in Figure 7.
